issues.description: The method Milkable.messageOnMilk() has inconsistent return types between the problem specification and the provided solution. Problem statement (UML and textual instructions) declares messageOnMilk() as returning String and explicitly states it "should return '[Animal Type] [name] is milked'". In the solution repository, Milkable.messageOnMilk() is declared to return boolean, and the implementing classes (Seal, Goat) implement messageOnMilk() to print the milk message to stdout and return true. This mismatch changes the method contract: students reading the problem will implement and use a String-returning method, but the provided interface/implementations return boolean and perform printing, which will confuse students and cause tests or example usage that expect a String to behave incorrectly.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature and behavior consistent across problem statement, template, and solution. Preferred fix to match the problem statement: change the interface to `String messageOnMilk()` and update Seal and Goat to return the formatted message string (e.g. `return "Seal " + getName() + " is milked";`) instead of printing and returning boolean. Update any call sites (e.g., Main and tests) to expect and use the returned String. Alternatively, if the boolean-and-print design is intentional, update the problem statement and UML to document the boolean return and the fact that implementations print the message, and adjust the exercise description and tests accordingly.
